newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe vows stamp out Corsica violence.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe vows stamp out Corsica violence.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said his government was determined to stamp out violence in Corsica after separatist guerrillas exploded 61 bombs on the Mediterranean island on Sunday in a show of strength.
Juppe vowed to pursue his government's crackdown on the guerrillas although he admitted there would be more bombings on the French Mediterranean island.
"We are fully determined. We enjoy the backing of the immense majority of our fellow-citizens in Corsica," he told radio France Inter in an interview on Monday.
"In time, I am convinced that the path or common sense, that is to say respecting the law and holding out a hand...will lead to a solution," he said.

No one was injured in Sunday's coordinated pre-dawn blitz and damage was mostly limited to smashed windows or damaged doorways at post offices, tax offices and other symbols of French state authority in towns and villages.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing, seeking to prove it had not been crushed by the detention of three political leaders, said it planted the 61 bombs and six others that failed to explode.
In a statement, it accused Juppe's centre-right government of betrayal by switching to repression from talks: "We will have multiple struggles, both in Corsica and in Europe."

It was the most violent night on the tourist island of 250,000 people since the Resistenza separatist group staged 50 blasts and attempted bombings on February 9 last year. More than 100 bombs exploded on one night in August 1982.

Police in the northern town of Ghisonaccia detained three suspected separatists for questioning about Sunday's blasts, which defied heavy police reinforcements and government pledges to end 20 years of violence on Corsica.
